headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: slim can read/write container artifacts and egress broadly while Superset can query APIs, creating a dangerous default handoff path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A and B have no documented shared clipboard, MCP, or filesystem bridge, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, slim can read/write filesystem artifacts and emits interactive CLI/stdout, while Superset exposes an API that could ingest content if an operator manually bridges outputs. This is an unusual, manual pathway, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an operator copies slim stdout or files into Superset inputs without review, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or message queue is introduced later, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste slim output into Superset fields without sanitizing it.
Disable any ad hoc file handoff between the tools.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on transferred artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: slim touches certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, and has broad network egress; Superset has allowlisted egress and an API surface. Even without a shared filesystem, a manual or scripted transfer of slim artifacts into Superset can expose sensitive data in default workflows. The pairwise leakage path exists, but not as an automatic shared-workspace default.
conditions: IF slim outputs certificate files, private keys, or env vars into artifacts that are later imported into Superset, leakage occurs.
IF Superset is configured to store imported content or query results, sensitive data may persist.
mitigations: Avoid importing slim artifacts containing secrets into Superset.
Redact keys and env vars before any transfer.
Restrict Superset datasets to non-sensitive summaries.
Review outbound destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce secret-scanning on handoff files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to mutable resources in practice: slim has write_filesystem and shell/subprocess execution, while Superset has an API and allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show shared locks or a shared directory, so high is not justified. Still, overlapping mutation of shared external resources is plausible if the operator points both at the same workspace or backend.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem or backend resource, write conflicts can occur.
IF Superset writes to a shared dataset while slim rewrites artifacts, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes to any shared backend.
Use read-only mounts where possible.
Check for concurrent jobs before starting either agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: slim can generate container-analysis outputs and Superset can consume API-fed data, so a common workflow is for B to render or act on A's results. The profiles do not prove B blindly trusts A, but no verification mechanism is documented either. That makes a default handoff error-prone enough for medium, not low.
conditions: IF Superset dashboards or downstream jobs use slim outputs as authoritative inputs, incorrect findings can propagate.
IF no human verification step is inserted between slim and Superset, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before importing slim outputs.
Label slim outputs as untrusted provenance.
Compare results against a second source.
Limit Superset actions to visualization only.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for imported findings.

E_compliance.rationale: slim explicitly handles certificate private keys, registry credentials, environment variables, and vulnerability data, while Superset has no documented compliance controls or residency guarantees in the profile. Because the pair can move sensitive operational data into a BI system, compliance mismatch is plausible. The evidence is docs-only, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or vulnerability data are loaded into Superset, retention and access-control obligations apply.
IF Superset is deployed in a different residency region than the source data, residency mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Superset.
Document retention settings for imported artifacts.
Restrict access to dashboards containing operational data.
Confirm residency for any hosted Superset deployment.
requires-engineering: map data-class handling to compliance controls.
